To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best linear unbiased predictor of the order statistic is the sample order statistic plus the sample average times the sample variance, and the best linear unbiased prediction error is the sample variance times the sample variance.

for a location scale family, the blu predictor of a future failure time is the mean of a weighted sample of past failure times, where the weight is a decreasing function of the rank of the past failure time in the ordered past failure times.
for the exponential distribution the blu point predictor of a future failure time is the sample median, whereas for the Pareto distribution it is the sample mean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of predicting the time to the next failure in a life testing situation when the underlying distribution function belongs to a location-scale family and is known up to scale and location.
the prediction of future failures in the life testing, reliability, and replacement situations, where the underlying distribution is unknown.
the problem of prediction in the context of a sample of independent and identically distributed random variables with known distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blu predictor is the sample quantile corresponding to the desired quantile level.
the best linear predictor of the order statistic of interest is a linear combination of all the order statistics of the past.
the proposed procedures are the most efficient in the class of linear unbiased estimators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give the blu predictors of order statistics in location and scale families and also provide large sample analogs for these predictors.
the blu predictors are the sample quantiles, but the blu predictors of order statistics are not the sample quantiles.
the blu point predictors are asymptotically efficient in the large sample sense.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best linear predictors for the time to future failures are the same for all distributions in location and scale families.
the blu predictor for the time of the next failure can be computed as a linear combination of the times of the first $k$ failures.
, for the exponential distribution, the blu point predictors of the order statistics are linear functions of the first few order statistics.
